label: prf:vertex-is-exceptional-divisor
html:
(1) Localisation. The braiding of \mathbf{C} is given by the universal R-matrix \mathcal{R} \in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g})^{\otimes 2} (R-matrix braiding), which acts on V^{\otimes n} by permuting tensor factors with a q-dependent phase. The Hecke generator is \sigma_i = \tau_i \circ R_{i,i+1}, where \tau_i is the transposition. Under the fibre functor \tau, the representation V is a module over the coordinate ring \mathcal{O}(G_q), which is the structure sheaf of the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) (the quantum flag variety of G_q at q). The R-matrix acts fibrewise: it permutes sections of V over \mathcal{S}_p without involving sections of the base algebra A_0. Hence \sigma_i is supported on \mathcal{S}_p.

(2) Confinement. The Skein relation L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})L_0 is the image of the Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 under the Markov trace. Since \sigma_i acts within \mathcal{S}_p (part 1), and the Markov trace is computed over the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p (the U(1)-bundle whose connection is \xi_q), every Skein resolution is evaluated within \mathcal{R}_p. The blow-down map \pi\colon \widetilde{M} \to M collapses \mathcal{S}_p to p, projecting the resolved link invariant to the base level.

(3) Completeness. The Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is generated by \{\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1}\} subject to the Hecke and braid relations. Every element of H_n(R, q) is a finite linear combination of products of these generators (braid action on tensor products). Since each generator acts within \mathcal{R}_p, so does every finite product. Crossing changes, pair creation (R-II moves), and virtual exchange are all expressible as finite braid words in B_n, whose Hecke images lie in H_n(R, q). No operation requires data from outside the blow-up.
